title: How Do You Change the Primary Admin in QuickBooks Online?
summary: How to change or transfer the primary admin in QuickBooks Online, including what to do when the current admin has left the company, the Simple Start exception, and firm-to-client transfers.
body_markdown:
**To change the primary admin in QuickBooks Online, sign in as the current primary admin, go to Settings, open Manage Users, make sure the new person is listed as an admin, then select Make Primary Admin and confirm.** The new admin accepts through an emailed link, and the transfer is done.


The whole process takes a few minutes when the current admin can still sign in. The harder part is every case where they can't.


The harder cases are when the current admin has left the company, when you're on Simple Start, or when an accounting firm needs to hand the role back to a client. This guide covers every scenario, step by step.


## Key takeaways


- Only the current primary admin can transfer the role to someone else.
- The new admin must already be a company admin before the role can move to them.
- On QuickBooks Online Simple Start, you have to contact Intuit to transfer the role.
- If the current admin has left, you file a Business Change Request with ID documents.
- A primary admin can't be removed outright; the role can only be transferred to a replacement.


## What the primary admin role is


The primary admin is the top user on a QuickBooks Online account. This person has the most permissions and controls everything the account can do.


By default, the primary admin is whoever set up the account. That works until the business grows, someone leaves, or an accountant who created the file needs to hand it back to the owner. At that point, the role has to move.


The primary admin has powers no other user has. They can add, edit, and remove users, change user roles, manage the subscription and billing, update company details, and connect or disconnect third-party apps. Because the role holds this much control, QuickBooks makes transferring it a deliberate, verified action rather than a casual setting.


## Why you might need to change the primary admin


The reasons fall into a few common buckets, and the one you're in changes how you do it.


The most routine case is a planned handover. The owner set up the account, an office manager or controller now runs the books, and the role should sit with the person doing the work. This is the easy path, because the current admin is available to make the transfer.


A second case is an accountant transferring the role to a client. Many firms create the QBO file during onboarding and hold the primary admin role temporarily, then hand it to the client once setup is done.


This sits alongside giving the firm[accountant access](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/accountant-access-quickbooks) to the books. It's common enough that QuickBooks Online Accountant has a dedicated tool for it.


The hardest case is when the current primary admin has left the company and can no longer sign in. A departed employee, a former business partner, or a fired bookkeeper still holding the role is a real problem, and it needs a different process entirely.


## How to change the primary admin when you can sign in


This is the standard process, and it works whenever the current primary admin still has access to the account. Follow these steps in order.


1. **Sign in as the current primary admin.** You must be logged in under the account that currently holds the role. If you can't sign in, recover your user ID or password first.
2. **Open Manage Users.** Go to Settings, the gear icon in the top right, then select Manage Users under Your Company.
3. **Confirm the new person is an admin.** Find the user you want to promote. In the Role column, they must be listed as Admin. If they're a standard user, select Edit and change their role to company admin first.
4. **Open the Actions menu.** Select the three-dot menu or Actions in the row for that user.
5. **Select Make Primary Admin.** Choose the option to transfer the role, then select Change Primary Admin again to confirm.
6. **Sign out.** After confirming, sign out of QuickBooks so the transfer can complete.
7. **Have the new admin accept.** The new primary admin receives an invitation email. They click the link and accept the role to make it official.


Until the new admin accepts, the role stays with you. Once they accept, the transfer is complete and they hold the top permissions.[Intuit's official documentation](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/primary-administrator/change-primary-admin-user-quickbooks-online/L9TU91iOk_US_en_US) matches these steps.


## The requirement people miss


There's one requirement that trips up most people trying to do this. The person you want to make primary admin has to already be a company admin. You can't jump a standard user straight to primary admin.


If the intended new admin is currently a standard or limited user, you have to edit their role to company admin first, save that change, and only then transfer the primary admin role to them. Skip this and the Make Primary Admin option won't appear.


This two-step setup exists on purpose. It makes sure the incoming admin already has broad permissions and isn't a surprise handoff to someone who's never had elevated access.


## The Simple Start exception


QuickBooks Online Simple Start handles this differently, and it catches a lot of small businesses off guard. On Simple Start, you can't transfer the primary admin role yourself through Manage Users.


Instead, you have to contact Intuit support to make the change. This is a limitation of the plan tier, not a bug. If you expect to transfer the role and want to do it yourself, it's worth being on Essentials or higher.


For a solo business owner who set up Simple Start and later brings on a partner or manager, this means a support call rather than a self-service change. Plan for that if a handover is coming.


## What to do when the primary admin has left


This is the situation that sends people searching, and it's the one the quick guides skip. If the current primary admin is gone and can't sign in to transfer the role, you can't do it through the normal settings. Someone has to prove they're entitled to take over.


QuickBooks handles this through a Business Change Request. You fill out Intuit's Business Change Request form, select the company, and submit identity documents that prove your authority over the business.


The documents you'll need include a government-issued photo ID such as a driver's licence or passport. If the previous owner is deceased, Intuit requires a notarised document naming the executor of the estate. Submitting the request sends an email to any other listed business owners or authorised parties, and Intuit reviews before granting the change.


This process exists to protect accounts. Because the primary admin controls billing, banking connections, and all financial data, Intuit won't hand the role to someone new without verifying they have the right to it.


It's slower than a self-service transfer, but it's the safeguard. It keeps a former employee from being locked out improperly and a bad actor from seizing an account.


## Firm-to-client transfers


Accounting firms have their own path for this, because they often hold the primary admin role during setup and need a clean way to return it.


From QuickBooks Online Accountant, sign in as the primary admin for the client's company, open the client's file, go to Manage Users, find the client, select the three-dot menu, and choose Change Primary Admin. The client then receives an email to accept the role.


This matters during[client onboarding](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/onboarding-bookkeeping-clients) , where a firm sets up the file, configures the chart of accounts, and connects bank feeds before handing full ownership back.


It's the same underlying transfer, done from the accountant's side. Firms managing many clients this way benefit from a consistent handover step, the discipline that lets them[manage 50 clients efficiently](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/manage-50-accounting-clients) .


## Can you remove a primary admin without a replacement?


No, and this surprises people. QuickBooks Online has no way to simply remove a primary admin and leave the account without one. The role can only be transferred to a replacement.


If the current primary admin is still available, the fix is to have them transfer the role to another active user. If they're gone, the Business Change Request is the only route. Either way, the outcome is a new primary admin taking over, never an account left with the role empty.


This is why it's worth reviewing who holds the role before anyone leaves. A five-minute transfer while the departing admin is still around saves a document-heavy support process later.


## Best practices for admin roles


A few habits prevent the worst version of this problem. The first is never leaving the primary admin role with someone who's about to leave the business. Transfer it before their last day, not after.


The second is keeping the role with the business, not an outside party. If your accountant set up the file and still holds primary admin, ask to have it transferred to you once onboarding is complete. You want to own your own account.


The third is reviewing user access periodically. Check who has admin rights, remove anyone who no longer needs them, and confirm the primary admin is someone currently at the company. Doing this alongside your regular[month-end close](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/quickbooks-month-end-close-automation) keeps access clean without a separate project.


Access hygiene is part of keeping your books secure, the same way the right[QuickBooks automation tools](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/best-quickbooks-automation-tools) keep the numbers clean. The primary admin controls your financial data and your banking connections, so the role deserves the same attention you give the numbers themselves.


## Conclusion


Changing the primary admin in QuickBooks Online is simple when the current admin can still sign in. Confirm the new person is a company admin, open Manage Users, select Make Primary Admin, and have them accept the emailed invitation. The whole thing takes minutes.


The complications come from the edge cases. The incoming admin has to be a company admin first, or the option won't show. Simple Start requires a call to Intuit rather than a self-service change.


And when the current admin has left the company, you're in a business change request with identity documents and a review. That's slower, but it exists to keep accounts secure.


The lesson underneath all of it is to manage the role proactively. Transfer it before someone leaves, keep it with the business rather than an outside firm, and review who holds admin access regularly.


A primary admin can't be removed without a replacement, so the account always has a top owner. Making sure that the owner is the right person before you're forced to turn a potential lockout into a two-minute settings change. Handle it early, and you'll never need the document-heavy version of this process.


## Frequently asked questions


### How do I change the primary admin in QuickBooks Online?


Sign in as the current primary admin, go to Settings, then Manage Users. Confirm the new person is listed as a company admin, open the Actions menu in their row, and select Make Primary Admin. Confirm the change and sign out. The new admin accepts through an emailed link to complete the transfer.


### Who can change the primary admin role?


Only the current primary admin can transfer the role. No other user, including regular company admins, can initiate the change. If the current primary admin can't sign in, the transfer has to go through Intuit's Business Change Request process instead of the normal settings.


### What if the primary admin has left the company?


If the current primary admin can no longer sign in, you file a Business Change Request with Intuit. You'll submit a government-issued ID and, if the previous owner is deceased, a notarised document naming the estate's executor. Intuit reviews the request and notifies other listed owners before granting the change.


### Can I remove a primary admin without assigning a new one?


No. QuickBooks Online doesn't allow an account to exist without a primary admin. The role can only be transferred to a replacement. If the current admin is available, have them transfer it. If not, the Business Change Request is the only way to reassign it.


### Why can't I make someone the primary admin?


The most common reason is that the person isn't a company admin yet. QuickBooks only lets you transfer the primary admin role to an existing company admin. Edit the user's role to company admin first, save it, and then the Make Primary Admin option will appear.


### How do I change the primary admin on QuickBooks Online Simple Start?


Simple Start doesn't allow a self-service primary admin transfer. You have to contact Intuit support to make the change. This is a limitation of the plan tier. If you anticipate needing to transfer the role yourself, consider upgrading to Essentials or a higher plan.


### How does an accountant transfer the primary admin role to a client?


From QuickBooks Online Accountant, the accountant signs in as the client's primary admin, opens the client's company, goes to Manage Users, finds the client, selects the three-dot menu, and chooses Change Primary Admin. The client then accepts the role by email. This is common at the end of onboarding.


### What can the primary admin do that other users can't?


The primary admin can add, edit, and remove users, change user roles, manage the subscription and billing, update company details, and connect or disconnect third-party apps. It's the highest permission level in the account, which is why transferring it is a deliberate, verified action.
